rationale: A wins because it respects the thin fact pack better: "Monzo Returns to the US, This Time Without Chasing a Banking License" turns the failed charter attempt into a clean strategic arc and names the proof before pretending victory. B is tighter, but "Monzo posted its first annual profit — then spent it on a second shot at America" smuggles in funding causality the update does not give. A still has a redundant regulatory angle and one underfed consumer explainer, but B asks the founder to pitch lines a reporter can kill in sentence one.
gaps_in_A: "Monzo's Partner-Bank Deal: What the Regulatory Structure Enables — and Where It Stops" is too close to "Monzo Returns to the US, This Time Without Chasing a Banking License." Same partner-bank-versus-license skeleton, just moved from company strategy to regulatory structure.

"What Monzo's US Checking Account Actually Is — and What It Isn't" promises the sharper half without the facts. The set admits it still needs "what the partner-bank arrangement specifically restricts," so the headline is ahead of the evidence.
"The prevailing narrative has been that neobanks sacrifice profitability indefinitely for growth" may be true, but it is outside the supplied update. It needs a cited comparator, not a knowing wink.
"Are any of the 9 million UK customers willing to speak on record?" is a soft proof ask for a US launch story. A UK customer is color, not the thing that makes the American product coverable.
gaps_in_B: "then spent it on a second shot at America" invents causality. The facts say first annual pre-tax profit and a US launch happened this year; they do not say profit funded the launch.
"renting a banking license" and "borrowed license" are cute, but legally loose. The supplied fact is a partner-bank arrangement; don't turn that into shorthand a bank lawyer can swat away.
"how the US entry playbook has changed" is a trend claim built from one company update. Either prove the broader playbook with other examples or call it a Monzo case study.
"home playbook survives America" implies a known UK playbook and a measurable transfer test. The update gives 9 million UK customers, not UK product behavior or US differentiation.
